title: What Assisted Evolution Labs Is
definition: Assisted Evolution Labs: labs accelerating species adaptation.
description:
Strip Assisted Evolution Labs to its essence and you get labs accelerating species adaptation. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Climate & Planetary Care: first evolution chambers understanding, then lab logistics prototypes, then genetic rescue operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of lab hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Assisted Evolution Labs
title: Real Research Today: Assisted Evolution Labs
definition: Today's documented research behind Assisted Evolution Labs.
description:
The road to Assisted Evolution Labs is already being paved. Ocean alkalinity enhancement pilots add alkaline minerals to seawater for carbon removal. Direct air capture plants (Climeworks Orca/Mammoth) operate in Iceland.

Enhanced rock weathering trials (Cascade, InPlanet) spread basalt on farmland. Together these programs form the evolution chambers foundation that Assisted Evolution Labs will build on — the lab logistics results, the genetic rescue methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as lab logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First governed lab hulls field trials: lab logistics monitoring
title: 2030 — First governed lab hulls field trials: lab logistics monitoring
definition: 2030 milestone on the Assisted Evolution Labs roadmap.
description:
First governed lab hulls field trials: lab logistics monitoring published openly, genetic rescue oversight in place.

What must be true first: the evolution chambers results have to replicate outside the lab, lab logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and genetic rescue operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed evolution chambers demonstrations, lab logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting genetic rescue uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Assisted Evolution Labs
definition: Estimates Assisted Evolution Labs readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Assisted Evolution Labs components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a lab hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Assisted Evolution Labs Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Assisted Evolution Labs operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Assisted Evolution Labs installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 15236 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where evolution chambers monitoring, lab logistics redundancy, or genetic rescue maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Assisted Evolution Labs Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Assisted Evolution Labs: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Assisted Evolution Labs — labs accelerating species adaptation.

Phase 1 — Prove (evolution chambers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (lab logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (genetic rescue): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (ethics): lab hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and conservation-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
